item.title: 23. Up to the Neck in Water: Why Peasants Rebel
item.itunes:title: Up to the Neck in Water: Why Peasants Rebel
item.description:
Tattooed rebels in Burma and burned tax rolls in Vietnam, 1930. James C. Scott's moral economy of the peasant: the drowning man, safety-first farming, the village as insurance, why fixed rents and head taxes were deadlier than larger shares, the Saya San rising and the Nghe-Tinh soviets, and the case for Samuel Popkin's rational peasant. First in the Scott and Fei series.

item.title: 22. Knives at the Veglia: How Violent Was the Premodern Village?
item.itunes:title: Knives at the Veglia: How Violent Was the Premodern Village?
item.description:
A misfired musket and an axe stopped at a church door. Six centuries of European homicide rates, a Tuscan village's 490 criminal cases, goats and crop damage, insults and the swords of the people, the village hard men who grew up to run the place, truces and peace treaties, Weber's French village wars and the prayer 'deliver us from justice', why violence fell, and how Italy went from Europe's most violent to among its calmest. Fourth in the Weber and Hanlon series.

item.title: 19. Peasants into Frenchmen: When Did France Become French?
item.itunes:title: Peasants into Frenchmen: When Did France Become French?
item.description:
Napoleon mistaken for a travelling salesman, a quarter of France not speaking French in 1863, and the schoolroom token of shame.
